Avery / team —

Summary of what we see so far (engineering):
- Root behavior: sudden traffic surge plus a sequence-length shift (median tokens per request increased ~2.3x) which pushed the serving runtime into a different kernel path. That kernel has higher memory working set and interacted poorly with our KV eviction heuristic, causing frequent KV cache evictions.
- Evictions caused repeated prefix recomputation and increased per-request compute; combined with the autoscaler spin-up lag this resulted in high queueing and 5xx timeouts.
- Additionally, a malformed healthcheck from a 3rd-party monitoring agent caused 1 of 3 warm nodes to be marked unhealthy briefly, reducing effective capacity at the worst moment.

Immediate corrective actions applied (complete):
1) Traffic was moved to a warmed variant (A/B fallback) — reduced error rate to <1% within ~9 minutes.
2) Disabled aggressive KV eviction threshold for BlueRibbon's pool to preserve prefix cached entries during peak windows.
3) Patched healthcheck parsing to ignore the 3rd-party header that was triggering false negatives (hotfix deployed).

Next steps (24–72h):
- Produce RCA doc and perf timeline (we're preparing a draft, attaching logs).
- Deploy conservative autoscaler policy for BlueRibbon during peak windows (config change + safety throttle).
- Run a controlled replay against staging with the same token-length distribution to validate kernel selection and memory behavior.

I'll attach the current perf logs and an initial timeline. We'll prep an exec-ready one-page with impact quant and recommended safeguards for your execs. 

Kimberly Park
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
